items.title: Cascadu interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, November 15, 2019
items.q: I mean Jimmy has mentored me in so many ways.

ctx.x: I have three in my basement.

Because the technology had changed. Nobody was recording on analog anymore, you know the studios were all set up for digital, all I had were my two boxes with my, you know, and I’m hauling these boxes and stuff, and it was Jon who took me to the studio to take all of that stuff and dump it into digital form. And he oversee’d the process when I would go into the studio, I would come home, I would stay by him and, this is what I got and he would check it out for me. I mean you couldn’t ask for any greater love man.…

when I was finished with that, and it almost took me out, I was really sick and everything, you know I called Jimmy and I said, “Jimmy,” ‘cause I always stayed in touch with Jimmy throughout the years. And I said, “Jimmy, I’m finished man. I’m tired of this thing. I’m not well you know, the school has taken me out, it’s going to take me a while to recover and everything else.” And Jimmy says, “Come in. Come let’s go play music.” And he put me on the bandstand right away. And I think that part of that is that…
